preamble: Labialization of the alveolar implosive through fusion with a following w: [ɗ] + [w] becomes [ɓ]. Gravina (2014) describes this as one of the most widespread fusions in Central Chadic: the stop closure and glottal component of *ɗ combine with the lip rounding of *w to give the bilabial implosive. Other languages instead keep only the glottal and labial parts, giving [ʔʷ]. Gravina calls the process sporadic and unpredictable, so it is a lexically conditioned change, not a regular sound law.
